source: Grierson, Linguistic Survey of India, Volume IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages (1906), Tūri section
edition: Original 1906 Calcutta printing, not a later reprint
rights: Public domain original (1906); Wikimedia Commons public-domain scan. Only two public-domain printed page images and factual transcriptions are packaged; the 701-page DjVu is a local cache.
scope: All bounded direct form/gloss examples and explicit controls in Tūri editorial discussion, printed pp. 128-129 (DjVu pp. 147-148); 24 individually inventoried units.
excluded_scope: Twenty-one inventoried items held: uncertain numeral diacritics, grammatical/inflected phrases, a conjectural emendation, a rejected comparison, and unstable Sarangarh pronouns.
The Aryan dative suffix ke and verb suffix discussion are grammar, not independent lexical records.
Tūri interlinear specimens beginning printed p. 130, and their free translations, are excluded wholesale; no word pair is inferred from narrative alignment.
Other LSI IV Munda sections and the Kaikadi/Korvi/Koda packages are outside this Tūri pilot.
method: Visually read source pages; Tesseract English OCR retained as a comparison hint, never authoritative for form diacritics. Every selected item manually checked against the printed page.
coordinates: The book gives district/state labels but no exact speaker or elicitation point. All three source-qualified dialect coordinates are blank.
etymology: No graph edges. Grierson's Santali comparison and conjectural reinterpretation of hor are editorial claims, not independently established links.
overlap: Existing compiled Turi has 269 rows. The three selected forms have zero exact form-plus-gloss overlaps in that file; the later Odisha witness is not known to reproduce this historical survey. See overlap-review.json.
